## 8. AUTOMATED TEST CROSS-REFERENCE

Automated coverage is tracked in the **Catalog Entry** column in Section 7, which maps each scenario to the feature-catalog leaf whose SOURCE FILES table names the regression tests.

A scenario file added or removed without updating Section 7 will show up as an orphan in the link audit, not as a silent gap.

Every file in this package also carries one `Provenance:` line at the end of its SOURCE FILES section, in one of two forms: `Provenance: <path to the automated suite that proves the scenario>` or `Provenance: manual only - <the command or prompt that exercises it by hand>`. The suite `runtime/cli/tests/playbook-provenance-paths.vitest.ts` walks the package and fails when a file lacks the line, uses a third form, or cites a suite path that does not exist.

Provenance: manual only - an operator runs each scenario linked from Section 7

content.text:
Hard rule: any critical-path scenario `FAIL` forces the feature verdict to `FAIL`.

### Release Readiness Rule

Release is releasable only when:

1. No feature verdict is `FAIL`.
2. All critical scenarios are `PASS`.
3. Coverage is 100% of playbook scenarios defined by the root index and backed by per-scenario files.
4. No unresolved blocking triage item remains.

### Destructive Scenario Rules

- Scenarios that delete or rewrite files on disk MUST run on non-production data only.
- Before executing, verify the affected resource can be rebuilt from scratch.
- Never run destructive scenarios in parallel with other scenarios that depend on the same resource.

### Root-vs-Feature Rule

Keep global verdict logic in the root playbook. Put feature-specific acceptance caveats in the matching per-scenario file.

---

## 6. SUB-AGENT ORCHESTRATION AND WAVE PLANNING

This section records coordinator/worker utilization guidance for assembling or reviewing playbook bundles. It is not a runtime support matrix and does not, by itself, prove feature parity for any CLI.

### Operational Rules

1. Probe runtime capacity at start.
2. Reserve one coordinator.
3. Saturate the remaining worker slots.
4. Pre-assign explicit scenario IDs, per-scenario files, and ranges to each wave before execution.
5. Run destructive scenarios in dedicated sandbox-only waves.
6. Record the utilization table and evidence paths in the final report.

### What Belongs In Per-Scenario Files

- Real user requests
- Orchestrator prompts
- Expected delegation or alternate-CLI routing
- Desired user-visible outcomes
- Isolation constraints or acceptance caveats that do not apply globally

# 475 -- ANCHORS_VALID nested anchor

## 1. OVERVIEW

This scenario validates the ANCHORS_VALID rule of strict validation on a Level 1 packet that `create.sh` scaffolded. The rule rejects an anchor that opens inside another open anchor, because a nested pair cannot be read as a clean section by anchor-based retrieval. The scenario first confirms that the scaffolded packet passes, then moves one opener inside another section and confirms that strict validation fails with the nesting finding.

### Why This Matters

A nested pair leaves the outer section's closer after an inner opener, so the two sections no longer end where their own text ends. The ANCHORS_VALID rule reports that shape at validation time, before it lands in the tree. This scenario proves the rule catches the defect and names the anchors involved.

---

## 2. SCENARIO CONTRACT

Operators validate a scaffolded packet, nest one anchor on purpose, validate again and read the finding.

- Objective: Prove that strict validation passes the un-nested scaffolded packet, then fails with exit 2 and `RESULT: FAILED` after the `risks` opener is placed inside `scope`, and that the ANCHORS_VALID finding names the nested anchors.

# Spec Kit: Feature Catalog

This document is the current feature inventory for the `system-spec-kit` engine. It describes the validation rules, templates and level contracts, spec-folder scaffolding and discovery, the continuity writer, generated metadata, phase decomposition, the doctor routes, and the workflow scripts that ship with the package.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

Use this catalog as the canonical inventory for the live `system-spec-kit` feature surface. The numbered sections below group the engine by capability area so readers can move from a top-level summary into per-feature files without losing implementation or validation context. Each section maps one-to-one onto a directory under `feature-catalog/`.

### What This Catalog No Longer Covers

The memory MCP server was removed: its 41 tools, daemon, launcher, plugin, hooks, database, embeddings, vector and BM25 search, causal graph, checkpoints, retention, ingestion, query intelligence, evaluation dashboards and ablations are gone, and so are their catalog entries. Nothing in this document describes those tools as available.

| Retired surface | Where the capability lives now |
|---|---|
| `memory_match_triggers` prompt-to-phrase matching | The generated trigger index, read by `node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lookup-trigger-index.mjs "<prompt>"` |
| `memory_search`, `memory_quick_search`, `memory_context` | The ripgrep recipes in [`references/retrieval/retrieval-conventions.md`](../references/retrieval/retrieval-conventions.md) §2, ranked caller-side per §5 |
| `memory_save` continuity writes | The packet-local continuity writer and `runtime/cli/continuity/generate-context.ts` |
| Session resume and context assembly | `/speckit:resume` over the handover document -> `_memory.continuity` -> spec-doc ladder |
| Daemon health checks | `node .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs advisor_status --workspace-root "$PWD" --format json` for the one daemon that remains |

Semantic paraphrase, vector and BM25 fusion, decay, access tracking and session dedup are a declared loss, not a relocated capability. `references/retrieval/retrieval-conventions.md` §1 carries the full boundary table.

---

## 2. TOOLING AND SCRIPTS

### Anchor integrity and nesting check

#### Description

Fails a spec document whose anchors nest, close before they open or close more times than they open, and ignores anchor markers quoted in inline code.

#### Current Reality

The rule runs inside the native validation orchestrator with the other anchor checks. Nesting findings are errors, and an adr-NNN anchor may hold adr-NNN-* anchors.

#### Source Files

See [`tooling-and-scripts/anchor-integrity-and-nesting-check.md`](tooling-and-scripts/anchor-integrity-and-nesting-check.md) for full implementation and test file listings.

---

### Architecture boundary enforcement

#### Description

Automates two import rules: `shared/` must not import from `runtime/` or `runtime/cli/`, and `runtime/scripts/` must contain only thin wrappers.

#### Current Reality

The checker runs over the surviving package tree and fails on a crossed boundary.

#### Source Files

See [`tooling-and-scripts/architecture-boundary-enforcement.md`](tooling-and-scripts/architecture-boundary-enforcement.md) for full implementation and test file listings.

---

### Canonical-first spec-root resolution

#### Description

Gives unqualified packet names a stable canonical winner, preserves explicit paths, retains a legacy-only read fallback, and blocks unsafe duplicate-root writes.

#### Current Reality

The resolver, collision classifier and write guard ship in `runtime/cli/core/`; the real-data migration and alias retirement remain deployment-gated.

#### Source Files

See [`tooling-and-scripts/canonical-first-spec-root-resolution.md`](tooling-and-scripts/canonical-first-spec-root-resolution.md) for full implementation and test file listings.

---

# Spec Validation Rule Engine

## 1. OVERVIEW

Spec Validation Rule Engine is the executable validation surface behind Spec Kit's documentation quality gates.

The engine has two parts with a firm division. `validate.sh` is a front-end: it resolves arguments and the set of folders to validate, then hands every rule decision to the compiled orchestrator at `runtime/lib/validation/orchestrator.ts`. The orchestrator detects the target spec level, runs the rules, and aggregates the result into terminal-friendly output or JSON.

The front-end deliberately implements no rules of its own. It used to carry a second, independent implementation of the same rule set, chosen between by environment; the two disagreed, so a packet's verdict depended on how the caller's shell was configured. One engine is the point.

---

## 2. HOW IT WORKS

### Entry Point & Routing

`validate.sh` first parses its CLI flags for JSON, strict, verbose, quiet and recursive modes, then checks two skip controls: `SPECKIT_SKIP_VALIDATION`, read from the environment or `.skilled/hooks/hook-flags.env`, and `SPECKIT_VALIDATION=false`. A skipped run runs no rule and exits 0. Under `--json` it still prints a report, marked `skipped: true` with one info entry and no errors, so a caller that parses the output is never handed an empty stdout. Otherwise it resolves the folder set and delegates. A compiled build is preferred; a source-only checkout runs the orchestrator through the TypeScript loader. When neither is available it exits `3` asking for a build rather than answering with a different rule set.

Rule inventory lives in `runtime/cli/lib/validator-registry.json`, which carries each rule's id, aliases, script path, severity, and category. The orchestrator implements the most common rules natively and shells out to the registry for the rest, so duplication is bounded to the handful implemented twice rather than all of them.

Rule selection is deterministic. By default every registry rule runs except those marked `skip`, plus the rules marked `strict_only` when `--strict` is passed. `SPECKIT_RULES` narrows the run to a named subset, canonicalizing aliases and hyphenated spellings. It selects *which* rules run and never *how* a rule decides, so a narrowed run cannot change a verdict on any rule it includes. A name the registry does not recognise is a hard error: a subset that matched nothing would otherwise report a clean pass for a packet no rule had examined.

Registry dispatch is guarded. For each rule the orchestrator resolves the real path, verifies it remains inside the rules directory (or the compiled validation directory for Node rules), and refuses anything that escapes. Shell rules report through `RULE_NAME`, `RULE_STATUS`, `RULE_MESSAGE`, `RULE_DETAILS`, and `RULE_REMEDIATION`, which the orchestrator converts into pass, warn, error, or info entries. Detail lines print whenever a rule produced any, because a finding that will not say what it found cannot be acted on.

### Quality Gates & Validation

Severity comes from the registry, not from a table in the front-end. Missing files, placeholders, anchor issues, table-of-contents policy, template-header mismatches, and spec-doc integrity failures are errors. Section, priority, evidence, and phase-link issues are warnings. Level declaration is informational. `--strict` upgrades warning-bearing runs into exit-code failure without changing the underlying rule outputs.

Level detection belongs to the orchestrator. It first looks for explicit level markers in `spec.md`, including `<!-- SPECKIT_LEVEL: ... -->`, metadata tables, bullet metadata, YAML frontmatter, or line-anchored `Level:` text. A `<!-- SPECKIT_LEVEL: review -->` marker selects the lean review-record path, which requires only `spec.md` plus `review/review-report.md` and waives the `plan.md`, `tasks.md` and `implementation-summary.md` requirements that apply to numbered levels. The review marker is the only entry into that path, so no inferred folder reaches it. If no explicit declaration is present, it infers Level 3 from `decision-record.md`, Level 2 from `checklist.md`, and Level 1 otherwise.

Phase awareness sits in the front-end. If the target folder contains child directories matching `NNN-*/`, recursive validation is auto-enabled unless `--no-recursive` is passed. The parent is validated first, then each child phase with its own detected level, and the run's exit code is the worst of them. A caller can declare exactly which children a recursive run must cover by pointing `SPECKIT_CHILD_MANIFEST_FILE` at a hashed manifest, so a child cannot be added or dropped without the declaration changing with it. In JSON mode each folder emits its own report object rather than one wrapper.

The engine therefore behaves as one validator with a thin front-end: a single place where rules are decided, a registry that names them, and optional recursive traversal across phased spec packets.

### Edge Cases & Caveats

The implementation extended the strict path beyond the original shell-rule inventory. `validate.sh --strict` now runs the continuity-freshness check (`32a180bba`), the evidence-marker lint wrapper built on the new bracket-depth audit parser (`7d85861a0`, `e40dff0bb`), and the scope-normalizer duplication guard (`ded5ece07`). That means the rule engine now enforces stale continuity timestamps, malformed `[EVIDENCE:...]` markers, and new duplicate `normalizeScope*` helpers in the same operator-facing strict run instead of relying on ad hoc sweep scripts alone.

A linked `upgrade-baseline.json` is not applied: its findings are not read, and the validator reports `UPGRADE_BASELINE_LINK` as a warning.

---

## 3. SOURCE FILES

### Implementation

| File | Layer | Role |
|------|-------|------|
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh` | Orchestrator | Parses flags and config, detects level, resolves rule order, sources rule scripts, aggregates results, and handles recursive phase validation |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/validation/continuity-freshness.ts` | Validation helper | Warns when `_memory.continuity.last_updated_at` lags `graph-metadata.json.derived.last_save_at` |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/validation/evidence-marker-audit.ts` | Validation helper | Bracket-depth evidence-marker parser used for audit and repair sweeps |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/validation/evidence-marker-audit.ts` | Validation helper | Strict audit that fails malformed evidence-marker cases |

### Rule Inventory

> **Representative subset.** The table below is an illustrative sample of rule scripts, not the full set. The authoritative, complete rule roster — including `check-ac-coverage.sh` (advisory `AC_COVERAGE`, default-on) — is the registry at `runtime/cli/lib/validator-registry.json`.

| File | Layer | Role |
|------|-------|------|
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/rules/check-ai-protocols.sh` | Validation rule | Rule script discovered and executed by the orchestrator for the AI protocols domain |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/rules/check-complexity.sh` | Validation rule | Rule script discovered and executed by the orchestrator for complexity matching |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/rules/check-files.sh` | Validation rule | Rule script discovered and executed by the orchestrator for required file checks |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/rules/check-folder-naming.sh` | Validation rule | Rule script discovered and executed by the orchestrator for folder naming checks |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/rules/check-frontmatter.sh` | Validation rule | Rule script discovered and executed by the orchestrator for frontmatter validation |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/rules/check-level-match.sh` | Validation rule | Rule script discovered and executed by the orchestrator for level matching checks |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/rules/check-level.sh` | Validation rule | Rule script discovered and executed by the orchestrator for level declaration checks |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/rules/check-links.sh` | Validation rule | Wikilink integrity scan over the skill's own markdown, registered as `LINKS_VALID`; also runs by hand over any skill tree |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/rules/check-normalizer-lint.sh` | Validation rule | Rule script discovered and executed by the orchestrator for duplicate scope-normalizer detection |

10: # Create Feature Catalog

12: `create-feature-catalog` is the feature-inventory workflow packet of the `sk-doc` parent hub. It authors canonical current-state catalogs rooted at `feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md`, with category folders and one per-feature reference file per root catalog entry.
13: 
14: Feature catalogs are the canonical inventory for what a system does today. They organize capabilities by category, summarize current behavior in a root catalog, and link to per-feature files that carry implementation anchors, tests, and metadata.
15: 
16: Core principle: use the root catalog for stable inventory and navigation, and use per-feature files for implementation truth and traceable source anchors.
17:

60: - Multiple docs need a stable source of truth for feature names and links.
61: - Reviewers or operators need one place to see what the system does now.
62: - Manual playbooks or specs need a canonical feature list to cross-reference.
63: 
64: Use a lighter alternative when:
65: 
66: - The system has only a handful of features.
67: - A README already provides a complete and stable inventory.
68: - The product is too volatile for a maintained catalog to stay accurate.
69: 
70: Decision rule:
71: 
72: ```text
73: Need a stable, reviewable current-state inventory?
74:   YES -> Create a feature catalog package
75:   NO  -> Keep capability summary in README or install guide
76: ```
77: 
78: ### Family Boundary
79: 
80: This is a nested workflow packet under `sk-doc`. It carries its own `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `references/`, `assets/`, and `changelog/`, but it must not define a packet-local `graph-metadata.json`; advisor identity lives at the `sk-doc` hub root.
81: 
82: ### Router Resilience
83: 
84: This packet routes by whether the target needs a stable, reviewable current-state feature inventory. It does not use runtime keyed resource discovery through `references/<key>/` because its references are flat.
85: 
86: - Load optional markdown resources only after resolving them under this packet and confirming they exist.
87: - Treat `references/README.md` as the fallback route map when catalog necessity or target feature scope is unclear.
88: - Ask for the missing target system, feature scope, or inventory requirements instead of silently loading no resources.
89: - Do not add a full `references/<key>/` or `assets/<key>/` runtime-key router unless this packet gains real keyed resource subdirectories.
90: 
91: ### Smart Router Pseudocode
92: 
93: For this flat-reference packet, the canonical resilient router discovers resources at call
94: time, guards and loads only what exists, scores the root-catalog vs per-feature-file intent,
95: and returns a disambiguation checklist rather than silently loading nothing:
96: 
97: ```python
98: from pathlib import Path
99: 
100: SKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
101: RESOURCE_BASES = (SKILL_ROOT / "references", SKILL_ROOT / "assets")
102: DEFAULT_RESOURCE = "references/README.md"
103: 
104: # Two routing targets; keywords come from this packet's activation triggers.
105: INTENT_MODEL = {
106:     "root_catalog": {"weight": 4, "keywords": ["root catalog", "feature catalog", "capability inventory", "catalog package"]},
107:     "per_feature_file": {"weight": 4, "keywords": ["per-feature files", "source anchors", "feature inventory", "/create:feature-catalog"]},
108: }
109: UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [
110:     "Confirm the target system, skill, or surface the catalog should cover",
111:     "Confirm whether the request needs the root catalog, per-feature files, or the full package",
112:     "Confirm where implementation source anchors and validation/test anchors live for the claimed features",
113: ]
114: 
115: def discover_markdown_resources() -> set[str]:
116:     docs = []
117:     for base in RESOURCE_BASES:
118:         if base.exists():
119:             docs.extend(path for path in base.rglob("*.md") if path.is_file())
120:     return {doc.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for doc in docs}
121: 
122: def _guard_in_skill(relative_path: str) -> str:
123:     resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()
124:     resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)
125:     if resolved.suffix.lower() != ".md":
126:         raise ValueError(f"Only markdown resources are routable: {relative_path}")
127:     return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()
128: 
129: def load_if_available(relative_path, inventory, loaded, seen) -> None:
130:     guarded = _guard_in_skill(relative_path)
131:     if guarded in inventory and guarded not in seen:
132:         load(guarded)
133:         loaded.append(guarded)
134:         seen.add(guarded)
135: 
136: def score_intents(request) -> dict:
137:     text = request.text.lower()
138:     scores = {intent: 0 for intent in INTENT_MODEL}
139:     for intent, cfg in INTENT_MODEL.items():
140:         for kw in cfg["keywords"]:
141:             if kw in text:
142:                 scores[intent] += cfg["weight"]
143:     return scores
144: 
145: def route_feature_catalog_request(request):
146:     inventory = discover_markdown_resources()
147:     loaded, seen = [], set()
148:     scores = score_intents(request)
149: 
150:     if max(scores.values() or [0]) < 4:                      # Tier 1: low confidence
151:         load_if_available(DEFAULT_RESOURCE, inventory, loaded, seen)
152:         return {
153:             "load_level": "UNKNOWN_FALLBACK",
154:             "needs_disambiguation": True,
155:             "disambiguation_checklist": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST,
156:             "resources": loaded,
157:         }
158: 
159:     intent = max(scores, key=scores.get)                      # Tier 2: happy path
160:     # Flat resource topology: no references/<key>/ subdirectories. The intent selects the
161:     # root-catalog or per-feature template already documented below, not a keyed subtree.
162:     for path in sorted(inventory):
163:         load_if_available(path, inventory, loaded, seen)
164:     return {"intent": intent, "resources": loaded}
165: ```
166: 
167: ---
168: 
169: ## 3. PACKAGE CONTRACT
170: 
171: ### Canonical Shape
172: 
173: ```text
174: feature-catalog/
175: ├── feature-catalog.md
176: ├── category-name/
177: │   ├── feature-name.md
178: │   └── another-feature-name.md
179: └── another-category/
180:     └── feature-name.md
181: ```
182: 
183: Invariants:
184: 
185: - Root file is always `feature-catalog.md` in lowercase.
186: - Category directories use descriptive kebab-case names such as `category-name` (no numeric prefix).
187: - Per-feature files use kebab-case names such as `feature-name.md` without numeric prefixes.
188: - One root entry maps to exactly one per-feature file.
189: - Slugs should remain stable after publication.
190: - Display order is owned by the root catalog index (`feature-catalog.md`), not the folder name.
191: - Per-feature snippet order is defined by the root catalog listing order; filenames do not encode order.
192: 
193: ### Required Resources
194: 
195: Use these packet resources while authoring:
196: 
197: - `assets/feature-catalog-template.md` for the root catalog scaffold.
198: - `assets/feature-catalog-snippet-template.md` for each per-feature file.
199: - `../shared/references/quick-reference.md` and `../shared/references/validation.md` before delivery.
200: - `../sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md` when checking frontmatter version fields.
201: - `references/README.md` to route the reference overflow — [`examples.md`](references/examples.md) (worked live-catalog walkthrough) and [`common-pitfalls.md`](references/common-pitfalls.md) (deep-dive pitfalls, template-versus-reference split) — only for depth beyond this inline workflow.
202: 
203: The source assets keep the filenames `feature-catalog-template.md` and `feature-catalog-snippet-template.md` until their separate source-file migration. Those filenames are authoring inputs, not emitted package names.
204: 
205: ---
206: 
207: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS: CREATION WORKFLOW
208: 
209: Follow this workflow in order.
210: 
211: 1. Read the target system docs, source files, command surfaces, MCP tool lists, tests, and existing README material before drafting the catalog.
212: 2. Decide whether a catalog is warranted; use a README summary instead when the feature surface is small, complete, stable, or too volatile for a maintained catalog.
213: 3. Decide the category taxonomy before writing prose.
214: 4. Stabilize category names, feature names, and feature slugs before polishing descriptions.
215: 5. Create `feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md` from `assets/feature-catalog-template.md`.
216: 6. Create one category folder per root section using a descriptive kebab-case slug such as `category-name`; the root catalog listing defines display order.
217: 7. Create one per-feature file for each root entry using `assets/feature-catalog-snippet-template.md`.
218: 8. Write concise root summaries and link each feature to its per-feature file.
219: 9. Fill each per-feature `## 2. HOW IT WORKS` section with current behavior.
220: 10. Use plain prose for short `HOW IT WORKS` sections and H3 subheadings for sections longer than three paragraphs.
221: 11. Fill implementation source tables and validation or test anchor tables for every feature claim.
222: 12. Fill `## 4. SOURCE METADATA`, including group, canonical file path, and related references.
223: 13. Validate the root catalog and each per-feature leaf file with shared validation (see §7).
224: 14. Manually verify feature-file links, root-entry parity, source anchors, and current-state wording.
225: 
226: Authoring order matters:
227: 
228: - Stabilize names and slugs before polishing prose.
229: - Finish root taxonomy before expanding file-level detail.
230: - Use implementation and test anchors to justify every feature summary.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 5. ROOT CATALOG REQUIREMENTS
235: 
236: The root catalog is the top-level inventory and navigation layer.
237: 
238: It owns:
239: 
240: - Frontmatter with title, description, trigger phrases, last updated date, and four-part version.
241: - A short H1 intro describing the current feature surface.
242: - `## 1. OVERVIEW`.
243: - Numbered H2 capability sections by category.
244: - H3 feature entries with concise descriptions.
245: - Current-reality summaries.
246: - Explicit links to per-feature files.
247: 
248: Root summaries should answer:
249: 
250: - What this feature does.
251: - What its current reality is.
252: - Where to find source-file and test detail.
253: 
254: Package highlights for root catalogs:
255: 
256: - Use frontmatter, including `trigger_phrases`.
257: - Include a short H1 intro.
258: - Do not include a Table of Contents.
259: - Do not use `<!-- ANCHOR -->` navigation comments.
260: - Start numbered H2 sections with `## 1. OVERVIEW`.
261: 
262: Do not overload the root catalog with:
263: 
264: - Exhaustive source-file tables.
265: - Full scenario matrices.
266: - Speculative future-state design.
267: - Long implementation explanations.
268: - Roadmap detail.
269: 
270: That information belongs in per-feature files, playbooks, or specs.
271: 
272: ---
273: 
274: ## 6. PER-FEATURE FILE REQUIREMENTS
275: 
276: Each per-feature file is the detailed reference entry for one catalog item.
277: 
278: Required structure:
279: 
280: 1. `## 1. OVERVIEW`
281: 2. `## 2. HOW IT WORKS`
282: 3. `## 3. SOURCE FILES`
283: 4. `## 4. SOURCE METADATA`
284: 
285: Each per-feature file must include:
286: 
287: - Frontmatter with stable `title`, one-line `description`, `trigger_phrases`, and a four-part `version`.
288: - At least three trigger phrases matching the H3 heading in the root catalog.
289: - An H1 matching the feature, with a tool or command name in parentheses when relevant.
290: - A concise overview of the feature.
291: - A behavior-focused `HOW IT WORKS` section.
292: - Implementation source tables with `File | Layer | Role` columns.
293: - Validation or test anchors with `File | Type | Role` columns.
294: - Metadata including group, canonical file path, and related references.
295: 
296: `HOW IT WORKS` subheading rule:
297: 
298: - Use plain prose when the section is three paragraphs or fewer.
299: - Add H3 subheadings when the section exceeds three paragraphs.
300: - Preferred H3 examples include `### Core Behavior`, `### Quality Gates`, `### Configuration`, `### Edge Cases`, and `### Async & Safety`.
301: - Describe behavior from the caller or operator perspective, not the implementation perspective.
302: 
303: Content rule:
304: 
305: - Describe behavior that exists now.
306: - If a rollout or compatibility layer is documented, label it explicitly.
307: - Avoid roadmap or speculative wording unless the feature itself is a documented compatibility or feature-flag surface.
308: 
309: ---
310: 
311: ## 7. PLAYBOOK AND VALIDATION BOUNDARY
312: 
313: Feature catalogs and manual testing playbooks serve different purposes.
314: 
315: | Document | Primary Question |
316: |---|---|
317: | Feature catalog | What does the system do today? |
318: | Manual testing playbook | How do we validate that behavior manually? |
319: 
320: Cross-reference rule:
321: 
322: - Playbooks should link back to the matching catalog entry when one exists.
323: - Catalogs should stay focused on current behavior, not test execution detail.
324: - Manual execution scenario matrices belong in playbooks, not catalogs.
325: 
326: Validation workflow — run from the repo root so the validator resolves the `feature_catalog` doc type on per-feature leaves (leaf detection accepts the canonical `feature-catalog/<category>/` path during the bounded compatibility window):
327: 
328: ```bash
329: # New-content naming guard. The staging root must contain only the newly authored
330: # canonical feature-catalog package, never an ancestor with shipped legacy roots.
331: python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/check_no_hyphenated_catalog_content.py <new-content-staging-root>
332: 
333: # Root catalog (detected as the readme doc type)
334: python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py <target-skill>/feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md
335: python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/extract_structure.py <target-skill>/feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md
336: 
337: # Each per-feature leaf (detected as the feature_catalog doc type; validates the Validation And Tests table taxonomy)
338: python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py <target-skill>/feature-catalog/<category-name>/feature-name.md
339: ```
340: 
341: The staging scope is mandatory until shipped underscore roots are migrated. Do not run this guard against `.skilled/skills` or another ancestor containing legacy `feature_catalog/` or `manual_testing_playbook/` trees.
342: 
343: The validator machine-checks the root-catalog structure and each leaf's Validation And Tests table, but not cross-file link targets or source-anchor accuracy. Manually verify:
344: 
345: - Every root entry links to an existing per-feature file.
346: - Every per-feature file is represented in the root catalog.
347: - Source-file tables reference real, stable paths.
348: - Validation or test tables reference real, stable paths.
349: - Catalog claims describe shipped behavior, not speculative roadmap.
350: - Cross-file links resolve.
351: - Runtime docs avoid mutable spec or phase packet history.
352: 
353: ### Package Validator Enforcement
354: 
355: `scripts/validate_catalog_package.py` is the package-level enforcement surface. Discovery is presence-based: every canonical `feature-catalog/` directory below `.skilled/skills/` is a package, keyed by its path relative to that root. The measured starting corpus is 26 packages and 804 leaves. The validator carries explicit runtime-data exclusion rulings for any root that could gain a same-named directory without a skill contract.
356: 
357: The validator compares root filenames and root-link targets case-insensitively. This preserves the `mcp-click-up` package's uppercase `FEATURE-CATALOG.md` without counting the root itself as an orphan.
358: 
359: The initial enforcement ladder is staged. Promoted packages fail closed immediately. The explicit WARN tier is `system-spec-kit`, `mcp-tooling/mcp-refero`, `mcp-tooling/mcp-click-up`, and `system-deep-loop/deep-research`, the four packages carrying the measured 104-orphan backlog. Repair children remove a package from the map when it is repaired; a clean package reports a promoted PASS. Use `--report-only` for advisory output; `--strict` remains an alias for the default.
360: 
361: The enforced roster is:
362: 
363: - root/leaf bijection and discovery coverage;
364: - SOURCE FILES path existence and Validation And Tests taxonomy;
365: - sk-doc workflow-mode parity;
366: - phantom root-row detection and repo-relative prose-path checking;
367: - root-H3-to-leaf-title parity and normalized description parity;
368: - packet-history metadata rejection;
369: - dark-vs-shipped labeling; and
370: - volatile measurement-snapshot rejection.
371: 
372: Catalog prose may describe structural rosters derived from links or source tables, but it must not freeze measured counts or dated snapshots. The validator reports those snapshots so the catalog stays current-state evidence rather than stale census data.
373: 
374: Validator boundary:
375: 
376: - `validate_document.py` checks root-catalog structure and, for per-feature leaves reached by a repo-root path, the Validation And Tests table taxonomy.
377: - Cross-file link resolution is enforced in CI by `check-markdown-links.cjs`.
378: - Per-feature link correctness and source-anchor accuracy still require manual review.
379: 
380: ---
381: 
382: ## 8. RULES
383: 
384: ### ✅ ALWAYS
385: 
386: 1. Use `assets/feature-catalog-template.md` for the root catalog scaffold.
387: 2. Use `assets/feature-catalog-snippet-template.md` for per-feature files.
388: 3. Preserve the canonical root path `feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md`.
389: 4. Name category folders with a descriptive kebab-case slug such as `category-name`; let the root catalog index own display order.
390: 5. Keep per-feature filenames stable after publication.
391: 6. Keep per-feature filenames free of numeric prefixes.
392: 7. Include source-file and validation anchors for every feature claim.
393: 8. Describe current shipped behavior from the caller or operator perspective.
394: 9. Keep the root catalog inventory-first and navigation-focused.
395: 10. Put implementation truth in per-feature files.
396: 11. Run shared validation on the root catalog and per-feature leaves before delivery.
397: 12. Manually verify cross-file links, source anchors, and root-entry to feature-file parity.
398: 13. Consume global standards and validators from `../shared/` instead of duplicating them here.
399: 
400: ### ⛔ NEVER
401: 
402: 1. Never add a packet-local `graph-metadata.json`.
403: 2. Never use a feature catalog as a roadmap unless future-state material is explicitly labeled.
404: 3. Never split one feature across multiple files without a clear category boundary.
405: 4. Never leave root entries without matching per-feature files.
406: 5. Never leave per-feature files unlinked from the root catalog.
407: 6. Never cite mutable packet numbers where current source paths, commands, or feature names should be used.
408: 7. Never use numeric prefixes on per-feature filenames.
409: 8. Never add numeric prefixes to category folder names; the root catalog index owns display order.
410: 9. Never use underscores in category folder or per-feature filename path segments.
411: 10. Never put manual execution scenario matrices in the catalog.
412: 11. Never omit source anchors for feature claims.
413: 12. Never leave long `HOW IT WORKS` sections as unbroken walls of prose.
414: 13. Never omit `trigger_phrases` from per-feature frontmatter.
415: 
416: ### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF
417: 
418: 1. The category taxonomy is unclear after reading the target system.
419: 2. Source anchors cannot be found for a claimed feature.
420: 3. The requested catalog mixes shipped behavior with planned behavior.
421: 4. Existing docs conflict about feature names or current reality.
422: 5. Validation fails in `../shared/scripts/validate_document.py` and the safe fix is not obvious.
423: 6. Published category or feature slugs would need to change without a deliberate rename migration.
424: 
425: ---
426: 
427: ## 9. COMMON MISTAKES
428: 
429: | Mistake | Why It Breaks | Correct Fix |
430: |---|---|---|
431: | Treating the catalog like a roadmap | Readers cannot trust current-state claims | Keep speculative material out or label it explicitly |
432: | Unstable renaming of category or feature slugs | Breaks links from playbooks and other docs | Keep published slugs stable unless there is a deliberate rename migration |
433: | Missing source anchors | Catalog claims become hard to audit | Add implementation and validation file references in the per-feature file |
434: | Writing execution-heavy scenario detail in the catalog | Blurs the boundary with playbooks | Keep execution matrices in playbooks, not the catalog |
435: | Playbook cross-references drifting from catalog names | Inventory and validation no longer match | Update catalog and playbook links together when a feature name changes |
436: | Wall of prose in `HOW IT WORKS` | Long unbroken sections lose scannability and navigation anchors | Add H3 subheadings whenever the section exceeds three paragraphs |
437: | Missing `trigger_phrases` in frontmatter | Feature is invisible to doc-trigger routing | Add at least three trigger phrases matching the H3 heading in the root catalog |
438: 
439: ---
440: 
441: ## 10. SUCCESS CRITERIA
442: 
443: The catalog package is complete when:
444: 
445: - The root catalog exists at `feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md` and was built from the packet template.
446: - Category folders use descriptive kebab-case slugs with no numeric prefixes, and display order is owned by the root catalog index.
447: - Every root entry links to exactly one per-feature file, and every per-feature file is represented in the root catalog.
448: - Each per-feature file carries frontmatter with a stable title, description, at least three `trigger_phrases`, and a four-part version, plus source-file and validation or test anchors for every feature claim.
449: - Prose describes current shipped behavior from the caller or operator perspective, with any rollout or compatibility layer labeled explicitly.
450: - Shared validation ran clean on the root catalog and each per-feature leaf, and cross-file links, source anchors, and root-entry-to-feature-file parity were verified by hand.
451: 
452: ---
453: 
454: ## 11. REFERENCES
455: 
456: The primary contract is this `SKILL.md`. Load the resources below only for overflow depth, worked examples, or schema checks beyond the inline workflow.
457: 
458: - `references/README.md` - route map for the packet reference set.
459: - `references/examples.md` - annotated walkthrough of a shipped feature-catalog package.
460: - `references/common-pitfalls.md` - deep-dive pitfalls with before/after fixes and the template-versus-reference split.
461: - `assets/feature-catalog-template.md` - root catalog scaffold.
462: - `assets/feature-catalog-snippet-template.md` - per-feature file scaffold.
463: - `../shared/references/quick-reference.md` - condensed commands and file locations.
464: - `../shared/references/validation.md` - shared validation and quality-scoring workflow.
465: - `../sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md` - four-part version field rules.

98: from pathlib import Path
99: 
100: SKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
101: RESOURCE_BASES = (SKILL_ROOT / "references", SKILL_ROOT / "assets")
102: DEFAULT_RESOURCE = "references/README.md"
103: 
104: # Two routing targets; keywords come from this packet's activation triggers.
105: INTENT_MODEL = {
106:     "root_catalog": {"weight": 4, "keywords": ["root catalog", "feature catalog", "capability inventory", "catalog package"]},
107:     "per_feature_file": {"weight": 4, "keywords": ["per-feature files", "source anchors", "feature inventory", "/create:feature-catalog"]},
108: }
109: UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [
110:     "Confirm the target system, skill, or surface the catalog should cover",
111:     "Confirm whether the request needs the root catalog, per-feature files, or the full package",
112:     "Confirm where implementation source anchors and validation/test anchors live for the claimed features",
113: ]
114: 
115: def discover_markdown_resources() -> set[str]:
116:     docs = []
117:     for base in RESOURCE_BASES:
118:         if base.exists():
119:             docs.extend(path for path in base.rglob("*.md") if path.is_file())
120:     return {doc.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for doc in docs}
121: 
122: def _guard_in_skill(relative_path: str) -> str:
123:     resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()
124:     resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)
125:     if resolved.suffix.lower() != ".md":
126:         raise ValueError(f"Only markdown resources are routable: {relative_path}")
127:     return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()
128: 
129: def load_if_available(relative_path, inventory, loaded, seen) -> None:
130:     guarded = _guard_in_skill(relative_path)
131:     if guarded in inventory and guarded not in seen:
132:         load(guarded)
133:         loaded.append(guarded)
134:         seen.add(guarded)
135: 
136: def score_intents(request) -> dict:
137:     text = request.text.lower()
138:     scores = {intent: 0 for intent in INTENT_MODEL}
139:     for intent, cfg in INTENT_MODEL.items():
140:         for kw in cfg["keywords"]:
141:             if kw in text:
142:                 scores[intent] += cfg["weight"]
143:     return scores
144: 
145: def route_feature_catalog_request(request):
146:     inventory = discover_markdown_resources()
147:     loaded, seen = [], set()
148:     scores = score_intents(request)
149: 
150:     if max(scores.values() or [0]) < 4:                      # Tier 1: low confidence
151:         load_if_available(DEFAULT_RESOURCE, inventory, loaded, seen)
152:         return {
153:             "load_level": "UNKNOWN_FALLBACK",
154:             "needs_disambiguation": True,
155:             "disambiguation_checklist": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST,
156:             "resources": loaded,
157:         }
158: 
159:     intent = max(scores, key=scores.get)                      # Tier 2: happy path
160:     # Flat resource topology: no references/<key>/ subdirectories. The intent selects the
161:     # root-catalog or per-feature template already documented below, not a keyed subtree.
162:     for path in sorted(inventory):
163:         load_if_available(path, inventory, loaded, seen)
164:     return {"intent": intent, "resources": loaded}
165: ```
166: 
167: ---
168: 
169: ## 3. PACKAGE CONTRACT
170: 
171: ### Canonical Shape
172: 
173: ```text
174: feature-catalog/
175: ├── feature-catalog.md
176: ├── category-name/
177: │   ├── feature-name.md
178: │   └── another-feature-name.md
179: └── another-category/
180:     └── feature-name.md
181: ```
182: 
183: Invariants:
184: 
185: - Root file is always `feature-catalog.md` in lowercase.
186: - Category directories use descriptive kebab-case names such as `category-name` (no numeric prefix).
187: - Per-feature files use kebab-case names such as `feature-name.md` without numeric prefixes.
188: - One root entry maps to exactly one per-feature file.
189: - Slugs should remain stable after publication.
190: - Display order is owned by the root catalog index (`feature-catalog.md`), not the folder name.
191: - Per-feature snippet order is defined by the root catalog listing order; filenames do not encode order.
192: 
193: ### Required Resources
194: 
195: Use these packet resources while authoring:
196: 
197: - `assets/feature-catalog-template.md` for the root catalog scaffold.
198: - `assets/feature-catalog-snippet-template.md` for each per-feature file.
199: - `../shared/references/quick-reference.md` and `../shared/references/validation.md` before delivery.
200: - `../sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md` when checking frontmatter version fields.
201: - `references/README.md` to route the reference overflow — [`examples.md`](references/examples.md) (worked live-catalog walkthrough) and [`common-pitfalls.md`](references/common-pitfalls.md) (deep-dive pitfalls, template-versus-reference split) — only for depth beyond this inline workflow.
202: 
203: The source assets keep the filenames `feature-catalog-template.md` and `feature-catalog-snippet-template.md` until their separate source-file migration. Those filenames are authoring inputs, not emitted package names.
204: 
205: ---
206: 
207: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS: CREATION WORKFLOW
208: 
209: Follow this workflow in order.
210: 
211: 1. Read the target system docs, source files, command surfaces, MCP tool lists, tests, and existing README material before drafting the catalog.
212: 2. Decide whether a catalog is warranted; use a README summary instead when the feature surface is small, complete, stable, or too volatile for a maintained catalog.
213: 3. Decide the category taxonomy before writing prose.
214: 4. Stabilize category names, feature names, and feature slugs before polishing descriptions.
215: 5. Create `feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md` from `assets/feature-catalog-template.md`.
216: 6. Create one category folder per root section using a descriptive kebab-case slug such as `category-name`; the root catalog listing defines display order.
217: 7. Create one per-feature file for each root entry using `assets/feature-catalog-snippet-template.md`.
218: 8. Write concise root summaries and link each feature to its per-feature file.
219: 9. Fill each per-feature `## 2. HOW IT WORKS` section with current behavior.
220: 10. Use plain prose for short `HOW IT WORKS` sections and H3 subheadings for sections longer than three paragraphs.
221: 11. Fill implementation source tables and validation or test anchor tables for every feature claim.
222: 12. Fill `## 4. SOURCE METADATA`, including group, canonical file path, and related references.
223: 13. Validate the root catalog and each per-feature leaf file with shared validation (see §7).
224: 14. Manually verify feature-file links, root-entry parity, source anchors, and current-state wording.
225: 
226: Authoring order matters:
227: 
228: - Stabilize names and slugs before polishing prose.
229: - Finish root taxonomy before expanding file-level detail.
230: - Use implementation and test anchors to justify every feature summary.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 5. ROOT CATALOG REQUIREMENTS
235: 
236: The root catalog is the top-level inventory and navigation layer.
237: 
238: It owns:
239: 
240: - Frontmatter with title, description, trigger phrases, last updated date, and four-part version.
241: - A short H1 intro describing the current feature surface.
242: - `## 1. OVERVIEW`.
243: - Numbered H2 capability sections by category.
244: - H3 feature entries with concise descriptions.
245: - Current-reality summaries.
246: - Explicit links to per-feature files.
247: 
248: Root summaries should answer:
249: 
250: - What this feature does.
251: - What its current reality is.
252: - Where to find source-file and test detail.
253: 
254: Package highlights for root catalogs:
255: 
256: - Use frontmatter, including `trigger_phrases`.
257: - Include a short H1 intro.
258: - Do not include a Table of Contents.
259: - Do not use `<!-- ANCHOR -->` navigation comments.
260: - Start numbered H2 sections with `## 1. OVERVIEW`.
261: 
262: Do not overload the root catalog with:
263: 
264: - Exhaustive source-file tables.
265: - Full scenario matrices.
266: - Speculative future-state design.
267: - Long implementation explanations.
268: - Roadmap detail.
269: 
270: That information belongs in per-feature files, playbooks, or specs.
271: 
272: ---
273: 
274: ## 6. PER-FEATURE FILE REQUIREMENTS
275: 
276: Each per-feature file is the detailed reference entry for one catalog item.
277: 
278: Required structure:
279: 
280: 1. `## 1. OVERVIEW`
281: 2. `## 2. HOW IT WORKS`
282: 3. `## 3. SOURCE FILES`
283: 4. `## 4. SOURCE METADATA`
284: 
285: Each per-feature file must include:
286: 
287: - Frontmatter with stable `title`, one-line `description`, `trigger_phrases`, and a four-part `version`.
288: - At least three trigger phrases matching the H3 heading in the root catalog.
289: - An H1 matching the feature, with a tool or command name in parentheses when relevant.
290: - A concise overview of the feature.
291: - A behavior-focused `HOW IT WORKS` section.
292: - Implementation source tables with `File | Layer | Role` columns.
293: - Validation or test anchors with `File | Type | Role` columns.
294: - Metadata including group, canonical file path, and related references.
295: 
296: `HOW IT WORKS` subheading rule:
297: 
298: - Use plain prose when the section is three paragraphs or fewer.
299: - Add H3 subheadings when the section exceeds three paragraphs.
300: - Preferred H3 examples include `### Core Behavior`, `### Quality Gates`, `### Configuration`, `### Edge Cases`, and `### Async & Safety`.
301: - Describe behavior from the caller or operator perspective, not the implementation perspective.
302: 
303: Content rule:
304: 
305: - Describe behavior that exists now.
306: - If a rollout or compatibility layer is documented, label it explicitly.
307: - Avoid roadmap or speculative wording unless the feature itself is a documented compatibility or feature-flag surface.
308: 
309: ---
310: 
311: ## 7. PLAYBOOK AND VALIDATION BOUNDARY
312: 
313: Feature catalogs and manual testing playbooks serve different purposes.
314: 
315: | Document | Primary Question |
316: |---|---|
317: | Feature catalog | What does the system do today? |
318: | Manual testing playbook | How do we validate that behavior manually? |
319: 
320: Cross-reference rule:
321: 
322: - Playbooks should link back to the matching catalog entry when one exists.
323: - Catalogs should stay focused on current behavior, not test execution detail.
324: - Manual execution scenario matrices belong in playbooks, not catalogs.
325: 
326: Validation workflow — run from the repo root so the validator resolves the `feature_catalog` doc type on per-feature leaves (leaf detection accepts the canonical `feature-catalog/<category>/` path during the bounded compatibility window):
327: 
328: ```bash
329: # New-content naming guard. The staging root must contain only the newly authored
330: # canonical feature-catalog package, never an ancestor with shipped legacy roots.
331: python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/check_no_hyphenated_catalog_content.py <new-content-staging-root>
332: 
333: # Root catalog (detected as the readme doc type)
334: python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py <target-skill>/feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md
335: python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/extract_structure.py <target-skill>/feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md
336: 
337: # Each per-feature leaf (detected as the feature_catalog doc type; validates the Validation And Tests table taxonomy)
338: python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py <target-skill>/feature-catalog/<category-name>/feature-name.md
339: ```
340: 
341: The staging scope is mandatory until shipped underscore roots are migrated. Do not run this guard against `.skilled/skills` or another ancestor containing legacy `feature_catalog/` or `manual_testing_playbook/` trees.
342: 
343: The validator machine-checks the root-catalog structure and each leaf's Validation And Tests table, but not cross-file link targets or source-anchor accuracy. Manually verify:
344: 
345: - Every root entry links to an existing per-feature file.
346: - Every per-feature file is represented in the root catalog.
347: - Source-file tables reference real, stable paths.
348: - Validation or test tables reference real, stable paths.
349: - Catalog claims describe shipped behavior, not speculative roadmap.
350: - Cross-file links resolve.
351: - Runtime docs avoid mutable spec or phase packet history.
352: 
353: ### Package Validator Enforcement
354: 
355: `scripts/validate_catalog_package.py` is the package-level enforcement surface. Discovery is presence-based: every canonical `feature-catalog/` directory below `.skilled/skills/` is a package, keyed by its path relative to that root. The measured starting corpus is 26 packages and 804 leaves. The validator carries explicit runtime-data exclusion rulings for any root that could gain a same-named directory without a skill contract.
356: 
357: The validator compares root filenames and root-link targets case-insensitively. This preserves the `mcp-click-up` package's uppercase `FEATURE-CATALOG.md` without counting the root itself as an orphan.
358: 
359: The initial enforcement ladder is staged. Promoted packages fail closed immediately. The explicit WARN tier is `system-spec-kit`, `mcp-tooling/mcp-refero`, `mcp-tooling/mcp-click-up`, and `system-deep-loop/deep-research`, the four packages carrying the measured 104-orphan backlog. Repair children remove a package from the map when it is repaired; a clean package reports a promoted PASS. Use `--report-only` for advisory output; `--strict` remains an alias for the default.
360: 
361: The enforced roster is:
362: 
363: - root/leaf bijection and discovery coverage;
364: - SOURCE FILES path existence and Validation And Tests taxonomy;
365: - sk-doc workflow-mode parity;
366: - phantom root-row detection and repo-relative prose-path checking;
367: - root-H3-to-leaf-title parity and normalized description parity;
368: - packet-history metadata rejection;
369: - dark-vs-shipped labeling; and
370: - volatile measurement-snapshot rejection.
371: 
372: Catalog prose may describe structural rosters derived from links or source tables, but it must not freeze measured counts or dated snapshots. The validator reports those snapshots so the catalog stays current-state evidence rather than stale census data.
373: 
374: Validator boundary:
375: 
376: - `validate_document.py` checks root-catalog structure and, for per-feature leaves reached by a repo-root path, the Validation And Tests table taxonomy.
377: - Cross-file link resolution is enforced in CI by `check-markdown-links.cjs`.
378: - Per-feature link correctness and source-anchor accuracy still require manual review.
379: 
380: ---
381: 
382: ## 8. RULES
383: 
384: ### ✅ ALWAYS
385: 
386: 1. Use `assets/feature-catalog-template.md` for the root catalog scaffold.
387: 2. Use `assets/feature-catalog-snippet-template.md` for per-feature files.
388: 3. Preserve the canonical root path `feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md`.
389: 4. Name category folders with a descriptive kebab-case slug such as `category-name`; let the root catalog index own display order.
390: 5. Keep per-feature filenames stable after publication.
391: 6. Keep per-feature filenames free of numeric prefixes.
392: 7. Include source-file and validation anchors for every feature claim.
393: 8. Describe current shipped behavior from the caller or operator perspective.
394: 9. Keep the root catalog inventory-first and navigation-focused.
395: 10. Put implementation truth in per-feature files.
396: 11. Run shared validation on the root catalog and per-feature leaves before delivery.
397: 12. Manually verify cross-file links, source anchors, and root-entry to feature-file parity.
398: 13. Consume global standards and validators from `../shared/` instead of duplicating them here.
399: 
400: ### ⛔ NEVER
401: 
402: 1. Never add a packet-local `graph-metadata.json`.
403: 2. Never use a feature catalog as a roadmap unless future-state material is explicitly labeled.
404: 3. Never split one feature across multiple files without a clear category boundary.
405: 4. Never leave root entries without matching per-feature files.
406: 5. Never leave per-feature files unlinked from the root catalog.
407: 6. Never cite mutable packet numbers where current source paths, commands, or feature names should be used.
408: 7. Never use numeric prefixes on per-feature filenames.
409: 8. Never add numeric prefixes to category folder names; the root catalog index owns display order.
410: 9. Never use underscores in category folder or per-feature filename path segments.
411: 10. Never put manual execution scenario matrices in the catalog.
412: 11. Never omit source anchors for feature claims.
413: 12. Never leave long `HOW IT WORKS` sections as unbroken walls of prose.
414: 13. Never omit `trigger_phrases` from per-feature frontmatter.
415: 
416: ### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF
417: 
418: 1. The category taxonomy is unclear after reading the target system.
419: 2. Source anchors cannot be found for a claimed feature.
420: 3. The requested catalog mixes shipped behavior with planned behavior.
421: 4. Existing docs conflict about feature names or current reality.
422: 5. Validation fails in `../shared/scripts/validate_document.py` and the safe fix is not obvious.
423: 6. Published category or feature slugs would need to change without a deliberate rename migration.
424: 
425: ---
426: 
427: ## 9. COMMON MISTAKES
428: 
429: | Mistake | Why It Breaks | Correct Fix |
430: |---|---|---|
431: | Treating the catalog like a roadmap | Readers cannot trust current-state claims | Keep speculative material out or label it explicitly |
432: | Unstable renaming of category or feature slugs | Breaks links from playbooks and other docs | Keep published slugs stable unless there is a deliberate rename migration |
433: | Missing source anchors | Catalog claims become hard to audit | Add implementation and validation file references in the per-feature file |
434: | Writing execution-heavy scenario detail in the catalog | Blurs the boundary with playbooks | Keep execution matrices in playbooks, not the catalog |
435: | Playbook cross-references drifting from catalog names | Inventory and validation no longer match | Update catalog and playbook links together when a feature name changes |
436: | Wall of prose in `HOW IT WORKS` | Long unbroken sections lose scannability and navigation anchors | Add H3 subheadings whenever the section exceeds three paragraphs |
437: | Missing `trigger_phrases` in frontmatter | Feature is invisible to doc-trigger routing | Add at least three trigger phrases matching the H3 heading in the root catalog |
438: 
439: ---
440: 
441: ## 10. SUCCESS CRITERIA
442: 
443: The catalog package is complete when:
444: 
445: - The root catalog exists at `feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md` and was built from the packet template.
446: - Category folders use descriptive kebab-case slugs with no numeric prefixes, and display order is owned by the root catalog index.
447: - Every root entry links to exactly one per-feature file, and every per-feature file is represented in the root catalog.
448: - Each per-feature file carries frontmatter with a stable title, description, at least three `trigger_phrases`, and a four-part version, plus source-file and validation or test anchors for every feature claim.
449: - Prose describes current shipped behavior from the caller or operator perspective, with any rollout or compatibility layer labeled explicitly.
450: - Shared validation ran clean on the root catalog and each per-feature leaf, and cross-file links, source anchors, and root-entry-to-feature-file parity were verified by hand.
451: 
452: ---
453: 
454: ## 11. REFERENCES

458: - `references/README.md` - route map for the packet reference set.

# Validation Rules Reference - Complete Rule Reference

Complete reference for all validation rules used by the SpecKit validation system.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### What Is This Reference?

This document provides comprehensive documentation for every validation rule enforced by the SpecKit system. It covers rule behavior, severity levels, detection patterns, and remediation steps for each validation check.

**Core Purpose**:
- **Rule Documentation** - Complete specifications for all validation checks
- **Fix Instructions** - Clear remediation steps when validation fails
- **Configuration Guide** - Environment variables and usage patterns

### Core Principle

> Validation ensures spec folders meet quality standards before claiming completion—preventing incomplete documentation from passing the Completion Verification Rule.

### Severity Levels

| Severity | Exit Code | Strict Mode | Description                       |
| -------- | --------- | ----------- | --------------------------------- |
| ERROR    | 2         | 2           | Validation failed, must fix       |
| WARNING  | 0         | 0           | Passed with issues, should fix    |
| INFO     | 0         | 0           | Informational, no action required |

CLI taxonomy: `0` = success, `1` = user error, `2` = validation error, and `3` = system error. `--strict` selects the rules that only run under strict; a warning stays advice in both modes and never changes the exit code. A rule that should block reports an error itself.

---

## 2. RULE SUMMARY

| Rule ID              | Severity | Applies To    | Description                                    |
| -------------------- | -------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `FILE_EXISTS`        | ERROR    | All levels    | Required files present for documentation level |
| `PLACEHOLDER_FILLED` | ERROR    | Core files    | No unfilled template placeholders              |
| `LEVEL_DECLARED`     | INFO     | spec.md       | Level explicitly stated in metadata            |
| `AC_COVERAGE`        | INFO     | acceptance-criteria.md | Advisory traceability scan over each criterion's Verification cell (on by default; `SPECKIT_AC_COVERAGE_ENFORCE=true` makes an under-floor result fail) |
| `AC_CLOSURE`         | ERROR    | acceptance-criteria.md | Closure gate for Levels 2/3/3+: unmet criteria block a completion claim, waivers must cite a real ADR |
| `CONTINUITY_FRESHNESS` | WARNING | completion claims | Opt-in strict-only completion freshness check |
| `ANCHORS_VALID`      | ERROR    | spec docs with anchored templates | Anchors present, paired and not nested (adr-NNN may hold adr-NNN-*) |
| `FOLDER_NAMING`      | ERROR    | Folder path   | Folder follows ###-short-name convention       |
| `FRONTMATTER_VALID`  | ERROR    | spec docs     | YAML frontmatter properly structured           |
| `COMPLEXITY_MATCH`   | WARNING  | All levels    | Content metrics match declared level           |
| `AI_PROTOCOLS`       | ERROR    | Level 3/3+    | AI execution protocols present                 |
| `LEVEL_MATCH`        | ERROR    | All files     | Level consistent across all spec files         |
| `SPEC_DOC_SUFFICIENCY` | ERROR  | spec docs, goal.md | Anchor sufficiency; for `goal.md` also the durable budget (one limit: fail past 4000) and binding-row existence |
| `FRONTMATTER_VALUES` | WARNING  | packet docs   | `contextType` or `importance_tier` outside sk-create-frontmatter's `frontmatter-values.json`; aliases are legal |
| `SOURCE_TAGS`        | WARNING  | research/ + review/ | `[SOURCE: path:line]` tags that name a gone file, a moved file or a line past the end, in packets created after the cutoff |

> **Partial reference:** The table above covers the most commonly-encountered rules. The authoritative, complete rule set and their canonical severities live in [`runtime/cli/lib/validator-registry.json`](../../runtime/cli/lib/validator-registry.json).

### AC_CLOSURE

`AC_CLOSURE` decides whether a packet may be closed. It is registered at ERROR severity and runs by default; set `SPECKIT_AC_CLOSURE=false` to opt out.

**Rule ID:** `AC_CLOSURE`

**Scope:** Levels 2, 3 and 3+. Level 1 keeps acceptance criteria inline in `spec.md` and is never gated.

**Rollout:** forward-only behind `SPECKIT_AC_CLOSURE_CUTOFF` (default `2026-08-30`), compared against the `Created` date in the packet's `spec.md` metadata table. A packet created on or before the cutoff, or whose date cannot be read, is advisory on **every** branch — presence, waiver integrity and completion alike — and is never blocked. A malformed override falls back to the default rather than being compared as a string, which would otherwise grandfather the whole repository. This mirrors the `CANONICAL_SAVE_CUTOFF` pattern rather than introducing a third grandfathering mechanism.

**Failure modes:**

### Patterns Detected

- `plan.md`
- `tasks.md`
- `acceptance-criteria.md` (if exists)
- `decision-record.md` (if exists)

- `**/scratch/**` - Scratch files are never scanned
- `**/memory/**` - Generated continuity artifacts use different validation (ANCHORS_VALID)
- `**/templates/**` - Template files are expected to have placeholders

## Metadata

|-------|-------|
| **Type** | Feature |

10: # Create README (workflow)
11: 
12: `create-readme` is the README authoring packet in the `sk-doc` family. It writes current-state folder READMEs from local evidence, using packet-local templates under `assets/` and shared create-quality-control validators under `../shared`.
13: 
14: ---
15: 
16: ## 1. WHEN TO USE
17: 
18: ### Activation Triggers
19: 
20: Use this packet when the request involves:
21: 
22: - Creating or refreshing a folder `README.md`.
23: - Documenting a project, skill, feature, component or source-code directory.
24: - Writing developer orientation for a code folder, including topology, boundaries, entrypoints and validation.
25: - Running `/create:readme`.
26: 
27: Keyword triggers: `create readme`, `/create:readme`, `readme`, `folder readme`, `write readme`, `README.md`, `front-page overview`, `code folder readme`.
28: 
29: ### When NOT to Use
30: 
31: Use another `sk-doc` packet when:
32: 
33: - The user wants to audit, validate, score, or optimize an existing README or another existing document without authoring or refreshing it. Use `create-quality-control`.
34: - The user wants to scaffold a skill, agent, command, benchmark package, feature catalog, testing playbook, flowchart, or changelog. Use `create-skill`, `create-agent`, `create-command`, `create-benchmark`, `create-feature-catalog`, `create-manual-testing-playbook`, `create-flowchart`, or `create-changelog`.
35: - The target is not markdown.
36: - The folder is self-explanatory and a parent README or inline comments already give enough orientation.
37: 
38: This is a nested workflow packet under the `sk-doc` parent hub. It owns README authoring only. It does not carry `graph-metadata.json`; advisor identity, skill graph metadata and cross-packet routing live at the `sk-doc` hub root.
39: 
40: ---
41: 
42: ## 2. SMART ROUTING
43: 
44: Route by artifact type first, then by folder purpose.
45: 
46: | Request | Output | Primary Template |
47: | --- | --- | --- |
48: | Project, skill, feature or component README | `README.md` in the target folder | `assets/readme-template.md` |
49: | Source-code folder README | `README.md` in the source folder | `assets/readme-code-template.md` |
50: | Skill package architecture document | `ARCHITECTURE.md` at the skill package root | `assets/architecture-template.md` |
51: 
52: This packet uses simple artifact routing. It selects general README or code-folder README behavior from request intent and target-folder purpose. It does not use runtime keyed resource discovery by project, stack, mode or model. The only packet-local resource groups are `references/readme/` and `assets/`.
53: 
54: Router resilience rules:
55: 
56: - Load optional markdown resources only after resolving them under this packet and confirming they exist.
57: - Treat `references/README.md` as the fallback route map when artifact type or folder purpose is unclear.
58: - Ask for the missing artifact type, target folder or validation expectation instead of silently loading no resources.
59: - Do not add a full `references/<key>/` or `assets/<key>/` runtime-key router unless this packet gains real keyed resource subdirectories.
60: 
61: ### Smart Router Pseudocode
62: 
63: For this flat-reference packet, the canonical resilient router discovers resources at call
64: time, guards and loads only what exists, scores the two artifact intents, and returns a
65: disambiguation checklist rather than silently loading nothing:
66: 
67: ```python
68: from pathlib import Path
69:

161:

164: ---
165: 
166: ## 4. README AUTHORING WORKFLOW
167: 
168: 1. Identify the target folder, audience and README type before drafting.
169: 2. Read the target folder contents, nearby documentation, package files, config files and existing commands.
170: 3. Do not invent commands, files, APIs, metrics, features or capabilities.
171: 4. Choose the smallest useful README shape. Use a general README for project, skill, feature and component roots. Use a code-folder README for source-directory orientation.
172: 5. Write current-state documentation only. Use stable file paths, commands, feature names and source links instead of packet IDs, phase IDs, migration history or temporary planning labels.
173: 6. Put orientation first: what this is, who it is for and how to use or navigate it.
174: 7. Apply progressive disclosure: title and tagline answer "what is this", overview helps the reader decide relevance, quick start appears only when there is a runnable path and detailed reference comes later.

183: ---
184: 
185: ## 5. GENERAL README OUTPUT SHAPE
186: 
187: A general README answers two questions: what this is, and how someone uses or navigates it.
188: 
189: Use only the sections that fit the audience.
190: 
191: | Section | Include When | Content |
192: | --- | --- | --- |
193: | Overview | Always | Purpose, audience, main value and prerequisites |
194: | Key Statistics | Useful facts help readers decide scope | Counts, version, supported modes or limits |
195: | How This Compares | Readers may confuse this with nearby tools | Short comparison table |
196: | Quick Start | Readers need to run or try something | Short setup, verification and first use |
197: | Features | Capabilities need explanation | Feature groups, behavior notes and examples |
198: | Requirements | Runtime, tool or service needs exist | Minimum versions, permissions and external services |
199: | Structure | Navigation matters | Directory tree and key files |
200: | Configuration | Settings exist | Config files, options, defaults and env vars |
201: | Usage Examples | Patterns are easier shown than described | Simple and advanced examples with expected results |
202: | Troubleshooting | Users can hit known issues | What they see, cause and fix |
203: | FAQ | Repeated questions exist | Short answers only |
204: | Related Resources | Links exist | Grouped skills, documents, commands or external references |

206: General README format rules:
207: 
208: - H1 is a plain title.
209: - Add a one-sentence blockquote tagline immediately after the H1.
210: - H2 headings are numbered and ALL CAPS, for example `## 1. OVERVIEW`.
211: - Numbered H3 and H4 subsections inside feature sections are ALL CAPS, for example `### 3.1 TECHNICAL REFERENCE`.
212: - Unnumbered H3 and H4 headings use Title Case.
213: - Name the feature or artifact in its heading: `### Spec Kit: a written record of every change`, not `### Powered by Spec Kit`.
214: - Emoji use follows two registers. The repository front-page README may use decorative emoji on section headings. Every other README uses semantic emoji only (✅ ❌ ⚠️ 🔒 🚨) for rules and status markers.
215: - Give every item in an inventory a description. A list of bare names says nothing about when to use each one.
216: - Keep paragraphs to 2-4 sentences. A passage with several distinct points belongs in bullets.
217: - Use `---` horizontal rules between H2 sections.
218: - Do not add a Table of Contents.
219: - Do not add `<!-- ANCHOR -->` navigation comments.
220: - Use tables for comparisons, file maps, configuration, options and troubleshooting.
221: - Use fenced code blocks with language tags.

223: Frontmatter is optional for normal project READMEs and recommended for skill or system documentation that should be discoverable.
224: 
225: ```yaml
226: ---
227: title: "[DOCUMENT_TITLE]"
228: description: "[One-sentence description]"
229: trigger_phrases:
230:   - "[search phrase]"
231:   - "[routing phrase]"
232: ---
233: ```

235: ---
236: 
237: ## 6. CODE-FOLDER README OUTPUT SHAPE
238: 
239: Create a code-folder README when a developer needs local orientation before editing the directory.
240: 
241: Include details when relevant:
242: 
243: - High-level purpose: what the folder owns.
244: - Architecture diagram: how callers, handlers, adapters and storage relate.
245: - Package topology: layers, zones and allowed dependency direction.
246: - Directory tree with only important files.
247: - Key files and responsibilities.
248: - Boundaries: what this folder may import, export or own.
249: - Data or control flow through important paths.
250: - Public entrypoints, exports or commands.
251: - Validation and test commands.
252: - Related documents.
253: 
254: Use this section model:
255: 
256: | Section | Include When | Notes |
257: | --- | --- | --- |
258: | Overview | Always | One or two paragraphs about current responsibility |
259: | Architecture Diagram | Helpful for dispatch, pipelines, adapters or layered flows | Prefer zones and arrows over prose |
260: | Package Topology | The folder has layers, zones or import rules | Show dependency direction clearly |
261: | Directory Tree | Always for multi-file folders | Show only important files |
262: | Key Files | Responsibilities are split | Table with file and role |
263: | Boundaries | Import rules or ownership matter | State allowed and disallowed edges |
264: | Data or Control Flow | Runtime paths matter | Keep to the main path |
265: | Entrypoints | The folder exposes APIs, commands or exports | Include function names, files or CLI commands |
266: | Validation | Tests or checks exist | Use commands that work from repo root |
267: | Related | Nearby docs exist | Link parent, sibling and architecture docs |

The blockquote tagline is the exception. It does not bind code-folder READMEs. This is a cross-reference to the single authoritative rule block, not a second list.

272: 
273: 1. Count the target folder's immediate subdirectories.
274: 2. When that count is greater than zero, include a fenced Directory Tree because the folder has nesting or layering. The validator emits `code_folder_directory_tree` when it is missing.

276:

280: 
281: - Document current behavior only.
282: - Use code terms exactly as they appear in files.
283: - Prefer file paths, exported names and commands over narrative history.
284: - Keep diagrams small enough to read in a terminal.
285: - State allowed dependency direction when the folder has layers.
286: - Do not force Quick Start, Features, FAQ or Troubleshooting unless the directory has runnable commands, meaningful capabilities or known reader problems.

292: 
293: Run shared validation on authored markdown when feasible:

320: - Included sections match the audience and task.
321: - No empty sections or placeholders remain.
322: - Section numbers are sequential.
323: - Local links use correct relative paths.
324: - Commands were tested or clearly marked as examples.
325: - Expected outputs are shown for verification commands.
326: - Code blocks specify language tags.
327: - HVR passes.

332: 
333: Always:
334: 
335: - Read the target folder and nearby docs before writing.
336: - Choose the README type before choosing a template.
337: - Keep READMEs current-state and reader-focused.
338: - Use relative links for local documents.
339: - Use fenced code blocks with language tags.
340: - Test documented commands when feasible.
341: - Show expected output for verification commands.
342: - Use tables for file maps, options, comparisons and troubleshooting.
343: - Keep `README.md` and `SKILL.md` casing intact.
344: 
345: Never:
346: 
347: - Add a Table of Contents or anchor-comment navigation.
348: - Leave template placeholders in the final document.
349: - Document commands, files or features not confirmed from workspace or user evidence.
350: - Cite mutable packet numbers, phase IDs or migration bookkeeping in durable README content.

352: - Create `graph-metadata.json` in this packet.

355: 
356: - No em dashes. Use commas, periods or colons.

366: - The target folder purpose or audience is unclear.
367: - The README would require product, brand or public-facing claims that are not in the repo.

195: | How This Compares | Readers may confuse this with nearby tools | Short comparison table |
196: | Quick Start | Readers need to run or try something | Short setup, verification and first use |
197: | Features | Capabilities need explanation | Feature groups, behavior notes and examples |
198: | Requirements | Runtime, tool or service needs exist | Minimum versions, permissions and external services |
199: | Structure | Navigation matters | Directory tree and key files |
200: | Configuration | Settings exist | Config files, options, defaults and env vars |
201: | Usage Examples | Patterns are easier shown than described | Simple and advanced examples with expected results |
202: | Troubleshooting | Users can hit known issues | What they see, cause and fix |
203: | FAQ | Repeated questions exist | Short answers only |
204: | Related Resources | Links exist | Grouped skills, documents, commands or external references |

207: 
208: - H1 is a plain title.
209: - Add a one-sentence blockquote tagline immediately after the H1.
210: - H2 headings are numbered and ALL CAPS, for example `## 1. OVERVIEW`.
211: - Numbered H3 and H4 subsections inside feature sections are ALL CAPS, for example `### 3.1 TECHNICAL REFERENCE`.
212: - Unnumbered H3 and H4 headings use Title Case.
213: - Name the feature or artifact in its heading: `### Spec Kit: a written record of every change`, not `### Powered by Spec Kit`.
214: - Emoji use follows two registers. The repository front-page README may use decorative emoji on section headings. Every other README uses semantic emoji only (✅ ❌ ⚠️ 🔒 🚨) for rules and status markers.
215: - Give every item in an inventory a description. A list of bare names says nothing about when to use each one.
216: - Keep paragraphs to 2-4 sentences. A passage with several distinct points belongs in bullets.
217: - Use `---` horizontal rules between H2 sections.
218: - Do not add a Table of Contents.
219: - Do not add `<!-- ANCHOR -->` navigation comments.
220: - Use tables for comparisons, file maps, configuration, options and troubleshooting.
221: - Use fenced code blocks with language tags.
222: 
223: Frontmatter is optional for normal project READMEs and recommended for skill or system documentation that should be discoverable.

225: ```yaml
226: ---
227: title: "[DOCUMENT_TITLE]"
228: description: "[One-sentence description]"
229: trigger_phrases:
230:   - "[search phrase]"
231:   - "[routing phrase]"
232: ---
233: ```

235: ---

237: ## 6. CODE-FOLDER README OUTPUT SHAPE
